title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia Minimal Residual Disease Detection: The Difference from Normal Approach
protocol: Add a low concentration of fixative to the lysing solution.
Simultaneously lyse and fix the sample using the modified lysing solution.
Wash the fixed sample to reduce background fluorescence from unbound fluorochrome.
Preserve the light scatter properties of the sample during processing.
Assess the quality of the acquisition and preparation of the sample.
Display data from each tube versus time or event number to confirm stability of the acquisition.
Choose a parameter sensitive to alterations in fluidic stability, typically with moderate to high signal intensity and on a laser different from the triggering laser.
Use CD45 APC-H7 as a good choice for monitoring stability.
Perform doublet discrimination to exclude coincident events or aggregates of cells.
Plot forward scatter in a two-parameter dot plot using area, height, and/or width.
Gate the singlet population after plotting forward scatter.
Assess sample viability by examining light scatter properties.
Plot forward scatter (FS) versus side scatter (SS).
Identify apoptotic cells showing initial loss of FS and gain of SS.
Monitor further degeneration with loss of both FS and SS.
Optimize the method to provide consistent light-scatter properties reflecting cell viability.
Set FS instrument settings properly to include nucleated erythroid cells during acquisition.
Use a viability gate to reduce background nonspecific antibody binding to compromised cells.
Include viable white cells without regard to nucleated erythroid cells.
Identify progenitors using CD45 and SS gating in the progenitor or "blast" area.
Include all events having CD45 less intense than the mature lymphocyte population for progenitor identification.
Exclude high-SS maturing myeloid populations from the progenitor gate.
Gating and coloring the CD34+ progenitors to directly visualize on CD45 versus SS plots.
Exclude CD45 very low to negative events as they consist of nucleated erythroid cells, plasma cells, aggregated platelets, and debris.
